title: An explicit splice-to-kernel-to-action family and its nonuniqueness audit

verdict.conclusion: Fibonacci splice deposits canonically supply nonnegative weights for a decimal log-frequency Gram kernel.  They also admit positive Euclidean nonlocal actions through spectral functions of the Laplace--Beltrami operator.  Two explicit inequivalent positive form factors fit the same splice data, proving that the sequence alone does not select a unique action or physical scale.

positiveKernel.proof: for every real coefficient vector c, c^T K c=sum_n deltaPi_n[(sum_j c_j cos)^2+(sum_j c_j sin)^2]>=0

actionFamily.euclideanAction: S_E[chi;g]=(1/2) integral sqrt(g) chi F(ell_*^2(-Delta_g)) chi
actionFamily.covariance: Delta_g is the scalar Laplace--Beltrami operator, so spectral functional calculus gives a diffeomorphism-covariant Euclidean quadratic form
actionFamily.positivity: F_A(z)>=0 and F_B(z)>=0 for z>=0 because every deposit is nonnegative

nonuniquenessTheorem.statement: the same splice deposits and decimal scales generate the distinct positive form factors F_A and F_B; therefore positivity, covariance and the splice sequence do not determine a unique quadratic action
nonuniquenessTheorem.witness: the recorded sample rows contain nonzero F_A-F_B

a Lorentzian prescription and proof of causality/unitarity or a declared nonlocal alternative
a field-content principle selecting scalar, tensor, spinor or gauge sectors

status: a precise positive candidate family and a nonuniqueness theorem are established; no unique physical action or measured constant is derived
